//: COMPOSITE (tree) fixture — PROTOTYPE. Proves the SEAM a container-only fixture skips: that the parent (`pa-btn-group`) drops its REAL children (`pa-btn` buttons) into the right place with the right nesting. Unlike a normal fixture, a scenario here carries BOTH `props` (the parent's own neutral props, mapped via this fixture's map = the button-group feature vocabulary) AND `children` (a list of NEUTRAL child prop-bags, each mapped via the CHILD component's map named in `childComponent`). Each wrapper's dumper renders the parent WITH the real child components composed in (keen: real `Button.button/1` outputs injected into the `button_group/1` slot; svelte: a tiny fixture-only `_compose/ButtonGroupComposed.svelte` that nests `<Button>` inside `<ButtonGroup>`), so the dump — and this golden — is the whole composed tree. This is a COMPARE-only artifact (correctness of the composed markup); the per-class contract still lives in button.json + button-group.json, so `check-all.mjs` SKIPS composite fixtures for the capability sweep. The child (`button`) is CONTEXT-FREE — the group passes it nothing — so the live-inject form keen uses is byte-identical to svelte's true one-pass nesting; for a context-COUPLED child (e.g. a tab whose `--active` comes from the parent) the same fixture would instead need a true one-pass render on both sides.
goldenConventions: The composed golden = the button-group `<div>` shell (with its modifiers) wrapping the real `<button class="pa-btn …">` children in document order. Both wrappers add `type="button"` on `<button>` (a golden convention also used by button.json). Attribute + class-token order and whitespace are normalized away, so goldens are written for readability.

features.//: The PARENT's feature vocabulary (button-group). Exercised subset only — the full button-group contract (nowrap, responsive variants, stretch) is asserted by button-group.json; this fixture is about the composition seam, not the class contract (check-all skips composites for capability).

scenarios.name: two-buttons
scenarios.note: The seam: group shell wrapping two real buttons. NOTE both wrappers DEFAULT a variant-less button to pa-btn--primary — so 'Cancel' (no variant) is pa-btn--primary, NOT a bare pa-btn. The standalone button.json never exercised a truly bare button (its no-variant scenarios all set themeColor/outline, which suppress the variant), so this composite surfaced that shared default.

scenarios.name: vertical
scenarios.note: Group modifier on the parent + two children (variant-less → the shared pa-btn--primary default) — proves the parent modifier and the children compose together.

scenarios.name: align-end-mixed
scenarios.note: Parent align modifier + children carrying their own variant/size modifiers — the child markup is the real Button output, not a placeholder.
